# fixtures/

`atomspace_builder_sync_feed.json` is a **real** sync-feed document produced
by `fincosys/accospace`'s actual
`atomspace_builder.exporters.gnucash_exporter.generate_feed()` — not a
hand-authored guess at the schema. It was generated by running that
function (as of commit `b33d445`, the tip of `main` at the time this
fixture was captured) against the exact `sample_hypergraph` fixture
defined in that repo's `tests/test_gnucash_exporter.py`, then serialized
with `json.dump(..., indent=2)`.

Reproduce it from a checkout of `fincosys/accospace` (formerly
`RegimA-Zone/fincosys-atomspace-builder`; the Python package it installs is
still named `fincosys-atomspace-builder`):

```python
import json
from atomspace_builder.builder import NeuroSymbolicHypergraph, NodeType
from atomspace_builder.exporters.gnucash_exporter import generate_feed

hg = NeuroSymbolicHypergraph("FINCOSYS_ECOSYSTEM_FIXTURE", 64)
hg.add_node("RST", NodeType.ENTITY, "Regima Skin Treatments CC",
            {"status": "Active", "entity_type": "CC"})
hg.add_node("PF", NodeType.PERSON_NODE, "Peter A Faucitt",
            {"status": "Active", "entity_type": "Individual"})
hg.add_node("ACC_55270035642", NodeType.ACCOUNT_NODE, "Regima Skin Treatments",
            {"account_number": "55270035642",
             "account_type": "Platinum Business Account",
             "currency": "ZAR", "entity_code": "RST"})
hg.add_node("ACC_55270018789", NodeType.ACCOUNT_NODE, "Pete Platinum Acct",
            {"account_number": "55270018789",
             "account_type": "Platinum Cheque Account",
             "currency": "ZAR", "entity_code": "PF"})
hg.add_edge("ACCT_OWN_RST_ACC_55270035642", "ACCOUNT_OWNERSHIP",
            ["RST", "ACC_55270035642"],
            roles={"RST": "entity", "ACC_55270035642": "account"})
hg.add_node("TX_55270035642_226_001", NodeType.TRANSACTION_NODE,
            "Scheduled Payment To J Faucitt Salary",
            {"account_number": "55270035642", "date": "2020-01-02",
             "description": "Scheduled Payment To J Faucitt Salary",
             "amount": -66137.66, "category": "PAYMENT",
             "counterparty": "J Faucitt Salary", "is_intercompany": False,
             "xero_account_code": "400"})
hg.add_node("TX_55270035642_226_002", NodeType.TRANSACTION_NODE, "Bank fee",
            {"account_number": "55270035642", "date": "2020-01-03",
             "description": "Bank fee", "amount": -50.0,
             "counterparty": {"name": "FNB", "type": "BANK"},
             "xero_account_code": "404"})
hg.add_node("TX_55270018789_227_001", NodeType.TRANSACTION_NODE,
            "Scheduled Pymt From P Faucitt Salary",
            {"account_number": "55270018789", "date": "2020-01-02",
             "description": "Scheduled Pymt From P Faucitt Salary",
             "amount": 66137.66})

feed = generate_feed(hg, generated_at="2026-07-21T00:00:00+00:00")
json.dump(feed, open("atomspace_builder_sync_feed.json", "w"), indent=2)
```

## Why this matters

`sync_fincosys.py`'s `--feed` path and `fincosys-atomspace-builder`'s
`GnuCashSyncExporter` were developed in separate repositories, by separate
sessions, against a shared written schema description
(`fincosys-ecosystem-sync` / sync-feed `schema_version: "1.0"`) — but
never actually run against each other's real output until this fixture was
added. `tests/test_atomspace_builder_feed.py` closes that gap: it feeds
this real exporter output through `load_feed()` + `build_plan()` and
asserts the plan comes out clean (no duplicate txids, no unknown account
refs, no unbalanced transactions), so any future schema drift on either
side of the repo boundary fails CI here instead of silently breaking the
sync at apply time.

## `commerce_shopify_rzl.json`

A real `fincosys-commerce-sync/v1` document: 109 Shopify order-header
records for Regima Zone Ltd (RZL), captured from the Shopify Admin API for
the store `regima-zone.myshopify.com` over 2026-08-01 → 2026-09-04 and
committed to `fincosys/entity-rzl` at
`accounting/shopify/raw-json/2026-09-06_orders_2026-08-01_2026-09-04.json`.
It is copied here verbatim.

`tests/test_commerce_import.py` uses it as a cross-repo contract test:
`commerce_import.convert()` must book every record, and the resulting plan
must come back clean from `sync_fincosys.build_plan()`. Regenerate it by
copying the current version of that file from an `entity-rzl` checkout.

Customer display names are present because they are part of the order record
and the entity repositories are private; no addresses, emails or payment
details are carried.
